answer: One defense is vouching with liability: a new agent cannot transact until an established agent posts a bond for it, and that bond is slashed if the newcomer is later caught colluding. The economy's trust atlas then maps who vouched for whom, so a river of fresh identities all tracing back to one sponsor stands out and freezes together. An attacker must either stake real capital on every fake account or build thousands of independent sponsors, which is like raising a dune one grain at a time.
